issue.title: Decide from tool_runs evidence whether to ship default tool_runs.soft_ceiling values for Codex and Grok

task_type_fields.proposal:
Decide, from `tool_runs` evidence, whether sase should ship default `tool_runs.soft_ceiling.providers` values for providers that have no hard synchronous ceiling (Codex, Grok, and any other provider where `SASE_PROVIDER_SYNC_CEILING_SECONDS` is unset). If it should, add them to `src/sase/default_config.yml`.

Background: epic sase-1cx added `tool_runs.soft_ceiling` (`default` plus per-provider durations, empty by default), exported as `SASE_PROVIDER_SYNC_SOFT_CEILING_SECONDS`. The Rust core budget is the smaller of the hard budget and the soft ceiling. Without either value, an agent's `sase tool run` keeps today's plain inline behavior and never escalates. So Codex/Grok agents get no inline-then-escalate unless a user configures a soft ceiling.

Suggested method: after at least one athena week of post-landing data, run read-only `runs.sqlite` queries (see research:202609/sase_tool_e6_e8_go_no_go §8) for agent-attributed `check` runs by provider. Look at duration distribution, signaled/killed runs, and kill→rerun pairs for Codex and Grok. If long inline blocks or provider-side timeouts show up, pick per-provider defaults (with rationale) and document them in `docs/configuration.md`. Otherwise record why no default is needed.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: "Default soft-ceiling values" was an explicit non-goal of epic sase-1cx (plan:202609/tool_run_escalation.md), and the landing plan lists this decision as an expected follow-up to be made from post-landing tool_runs evidence, which does not exist yet at landing time.

issue.creation_reason: Epic sase-1cx shipped the soft-ceiling config empty by default, so providers without a hard ceiling never escalate; the plan deferred choosing defaults until post-landing tool_runs evidence exists.
